content: Information retrieval is the process of obtaining information system resources relevant to an information need from a collection. It covers searching within documents, databases, and the internet.
Machine learning models can be used for various tasks including classification, regression, and clustering. Neural networks are one of the most powerful machine learning techniques.
Natural language processing is a subfield of artificial intelligence that deals with the interaction between computers and humans using natural language.
Dense vector retrieval uses neural encoders to map text into high-dimensional embedding spaces where semantic similarity can be measured by cosine or dot-product distance.
SPLADE is a sparse retrieval model that learns importance weights for BERT vocabulary terms, producing sparse representations that can be efficiently indexed with inverted indexes.
Hybrid search combines sparse and dense retrieval signals to achieve better recall and precision than either method alone. Fusion strategies include linear combination and reciprocal rank fusion.
Graph-based document expansion leverages document-document similarity graphs to improve retrieval by incorporating neighborhood information and multi-hop relationships.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines information retrieval with large language model generation to produce factual, grounded answers to user queries.
FAISS is a library for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors developed by Facebook AI Research. It supports multiple indexing strategies including IVF and HNSW.
Elasticsearch provides full-text search and BM25 scoring as well as support for semantic search through vector fields and rank_features for sparse neural representations.
Sentence transformers are models fine-tuned with contrastive learning objectives to produce semantically meaningful sentence embeddings useful for retrieval tasks.
BM25 is a probabilistic retrieval model based on term frequency and inverse document frequency that has been a strong baseline for sparse retrieval for decades.
HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) graphs enable approximate nearest neighbor search in high-dimensional spaces with logarithmic query time complexity.
Quantization reduces the memory footprint of vector indexes by representing floating point values with fewer bits, enabling faster search with minimal accuracy loss.
PostgreSQL with GIN indexes can be used for full-text search and sparse vector storage, providing a relational database alternative to dedicated search engines.
